title: Factory project settings
description: Settings of the factory plugin for one project, in .factory/settings.json. Written by you, or by the /factory orchestrator when you ask for or approve a change. Missing keys take the default shown here. Reference: plugins/factory/skills/factory/reference/settings.md.

$schema.description: JSON Schema of this file, for editor completion and checks.

agents.description: Default model and effort of each agent. model-router routes a task away from these only when the task calls for it; with routing.mode "defaults" agents always run at these values.

mode.description: auto: model-router adapts model and effort to each task. defaults: agents always run at their agents values; model-router runs only to escalate a task that keeps failing.

until.description: Where /factory new stops when no --until is given. build runs every phase without pausing.

pacing.description: Where a build run pauses: after each task (a parallel batch counts as one), after each plan phase, or never. --through and --until override it for one run.

parallel_tasks.description: Run tasks the plan marks parallel_with side by side. false: one task at a time.

gate_order.description: After test-runner passes: run the other gates side by side (faster), or one at a time, ending the round at the first FAIL (cheaper).

decisions.description: Who answers the questions raised after discover (major ADRs, spec approval, agents' questions, changes, stuck loops, retro proposals). agent: the decision agent decides, logs each answer and its reasons in decision-log.md for you to review or override, and asks you only what needs your judgement. user: you answer every one. Setup, intake, discover and the greenfield foundation always ask you.

docs.description: Run docs-writer when a task that changes documented behavior closes. Tasks of type docs always run.

retro.description: Run retro-analyst at each phase close. false also skips the review of the non-blocking notes it surfaces.

escalate_after.description: FAILs of the same gate on a task before model-router escalates it (stronger model or effort, debugger, split, or an upstream fix), and before a repeated security FAIL asks you to freeze the scope. Must be lower than ask_after.

ask_after.description: FAILs of the same gate on a task, or rounds of the same review loop, before the factory stops and asks you.

debugger.description: Escalating a repeated test-runner FAIL routes the debugger. false: escalation picks another remedy.

environment.description: Failures caused by tooling or the environment: fix them when trivial and ask otherwise, or always ask.

exposure.description: Who can reach the software. private: only you or your team, no untrusted input. internal: trusted users, for example on a company network. public: the internet, or people you do not know. The security review weighs exploits against it; /factory setup uses it to preset checks.

checks.description: What the security review looks for. A finding in a disabled family is at most a non-blocking note.

untrusted_input.description: Files, clipboard, URLs, IPC payloads, plugin input, imported documents.

injection.description: Shell, SQL, path traversal, HTML or script in rendered content, format strings.

privilege.description: Commands, endpoints, capabilities or permissions broader than needed.

filesystem.description: Writes outside intended directories, symlinks, temp-file races, permissions.

secrets.description: Keys or tokens in code, logs, errors or config.

memory_safety.description: unsafe blocks, FFI, unchecked indexing, integer overflow on sizes.

denial_of_service.description: Unbounded loops, recursion or allocation driven by untrusted input.

dependencies.description: Advisories, maintenance and install scripts of new dependencies.

depth.description: minimal: one test case per spec item (main path and main error). standard: each item and the edge cases its criteria list. thorough: also boundaries, adversarial inputs, and property tests wherever they fit.

levels.description: Test levels the factory may use; at least one must be true. Items only a disabled level could prove are listed as untested.

property.description: Generated inputs for math, parsers and round-trips.

integration.description: Module boundaries, IPC, the real entry point.

e2e.description: User flows through the running app; false also skips the phase-close acceptance run.

gates.description: When each optional gate runs: off (never), auto (on tasks that match its trigger), always (on every task with production code). test-runner and code-reviewer always run.

security-reviewer.description: Security review of the diff, limited to the families enabled in security.checks. auto: tasks that handle external input, files, IPC, network, permissions or secrets.

dependency-auditor.description: Audit of added or upgraded dependencies. auto: tasks that change a manifest or lockfile.

perf-reviewer.description: Performance review of hot paths. auto: tasks that implement an NFR performance item.

ui-reviewer.description: Visual review against the spec and design system. auto: tasks that change UI.

ux-reviewer.description: Interaction design review. auto: tasks that change UI.

a11y-reviewer.description: Accessibility review. auto: tasks that change UI.

spec-auditor.description: Spec drift check on a task. auto: size M tasks and tasks that touch a contract. The phase-close audit always runs.

commands.description: The project's commands, when you want to fix them. Empty: test-strategist finds them for each feature.

test_one.description: One test file; <file> stands for its path.

model.description: haiku: mechanical work with deterministic checks. sonnet: well-specified local work. opus: judgement, design, hard reasoning.

effort.description: Reasoning effort; low only for mechanical work.
